# rustinion_group_active_response (Resource)

Manages a group's active response. A detection rule match at or above `min_level` can block the attacking address on the device's firewall for a while, kill the process the log line names, or lock a newly created account. Starts in dry run (it only records what it would do). Never touched: private ranges (unless allowed), the allowlist, admins' recent addresses, the Rustinion server, root/Administrator and protected accounts. Blocks and locks expire; every applied action can be undone. Destroying this resource turns active response off.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) The group these settings belong to.

### Optional

- `allowlist` (List of String) Addresses and CIDR ranges that are never blocked (your offices and VPN). Default none.
- `block_ip` (Boolean) Block the source address on the host firewall. Default true.
- `block_minutes` (Number) How long a block lasts (1 to 10080). Default 60.
- `block_private` (Boolean) Allow blocking private address ranges (RFC 1918, ULA). Default false.
- `disable_hours` (Number) How long an account lock lasts in hours (0 = until undone, at most 720). Default 24.
- `disable_user` (Boolean) Lock a newly created account a rule flagged. Default false.
- `dry_run` (Boolean) Only record what would be done. Default true: set false when the dry-run log looks right.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Turn active response on for the group. Default true (the resource exists to turn it on).
- `kill_process` (Boolean) Kill the process a matched log line names (pid and name must still match). Default false.
- `min_level` (String) Act on matches of at least this level (low, medium, high, critical). Default high.
- `protected_users` (List of String) Accounts that are never locked (root and Administrator always are protected). Default none.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as group_id.
